doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Bix Beiderbecke remembered
summary: Gallodoro heard Bix only in concert in 1927; Willcox played with him about nine months in the Goldkette band; both praise his style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Can you tell me a little bit about Bix, and what you remember?
No, the only time I heard Bix was at the St. Charles Theater in concert. But I never met him.
He died in 1931. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
I missed something good that night. The next day I found out that Frankie Trumbauer and Bix were all over Bourbon Street sitting in with different groups but I didn’t know about this.

1927 Yeah. See the Goldkette band split for a reference number say Labor Day of 1927. That is when the Goldkette, the Victor band I mean that it was known, and so my portion, but I played with Bix Beiderbecke in the Goldkette band for about nine months out of his short life. He died when he was 28 and if he’d a hung out with me, he’d a been 92 now too.
You know Bix didn’t play with a lot of notes, but what a style, what a style. Beautiful. He swung.
Yeah. And he influenced people after him also.
